answer: Shale-Grove Mirror Decay: each identity’s reward weight is a mirror of its provenance closure. A clone inherits the parent’s closure; until it accumulates k disjoint grove neighbors (counterparties not reachable from parent), its outputs pass through a shale cooldown with decaying reward weight. Self-dealing is rejected by closure-intersection checks. Cost: k genuine external interactions plus cooldown compute/opportunity cost; marginal clone payout stays below that, so EV<0.
